trace: The question is whether SHOP is about to break out or break down over a 1-7 day window. The evidence is tightly stacked around one dominant signal: a Bollinger Band Squeeze, with BandWidth at just 4.5% -- historically in the 12th percentile. That extreme compression almost guarantees an imminent volatility expansion, but says nothing about direction. Price at 65.10 is essentially glued to both the 20-day EMA (65.05) and the 20-day SMA (64.80), which reinforces the point -- the market has reached near-perfect equilibrium. RSI at 49.5 and a near-flat MACD histogram (-0.21 vs -0.23 signal) confirm zero directional momentum right now. The tension is that the squeeze setup is high-conviction while the direction is coin-flip. Fundamentals add a modest directional lean. A forward P/E of 62.1x and P/S of 8.5x mean SHOP is priced for perfection -- any macro wobble or guidance miss gets punished severely, which historically skews post-squeeze moves toward the downside in richly valued names. That said, 23% YoY revenue growth and recently achieved GAAP profitability are legitimate supports. The 50-day EMA at 68.20 stands as meaningful overhead resistance; the real downside pivot is 62.50, below which 58.00 (the 200-day SMA) opens up. My read: do not take a directional position yet. Wait for a confirmed daily close above 66.25 (upper band) with volume expansion for a long entry, or below 63.35 and 62.50 for a short. ATR is compressed at 1.80 but will expand. Confidence in the impending volatility expansion is high; confidence in direction is not.

PLTR at 24.85 is showing classic post-rally consolidation signals. On the hourly chart, the MACD has just crossed bearish (line 0.12 below signal 0.15, histogram turning negative at -0.03), RSI has cooled to 52.3 from overbought above 70 earlier in the week, and small spinning-top candles confirm indecision. Price is caught between the 20-hour EMA at 24.70 (support that may give way) and the recent swing high at 25.50. The structural read is moderately bearish short-term, but not aggressively so. The 50-hour SMA at 24.10 is the real line in the sand -- that level coincides with a volume shelf and represents a potential 3% drop from current levels, meaningful for a 1-7 day hold. The key tension is between bearish near-term technicals and PLTR's chronic squeeze potential: beta is 1.9 and any positive market shift could rip to 26.00 fast, a scenario assigned 40% probability. Options data adds nuance: high open interest at the 25 strike for weekly expiration means market makers have incentive to pin price near that level into Friday, which actually argues against a clean breakdown before expiration. The tactical short setup makes sense only on a confirmed hourly close below 24.70. Entry there, target 24.10, stop above 25.05 gives roughly a 2:1 risk-reward. A breakdown below 24.10 opens 23.00, a 7.5% drawdown from current price. The probability assigned to that breakdown scenario is 35%. Overall stance is short-term bearish lean with medium conviction, contingent on the 24.70 level giving way.

KO is a long-term value analysis, so the real question is whether the stock merits a 12-plus month hold at 62.50. The fundamental profile is compelling. ROE of 43.5% dwarfs the sector median of 15% and reflects the power of Coca-Cola brand equity as a durable economic moat. Net profit margin of 23.8% is best-in-class among consumer staples. Revenue grew 5.8% YoY -- modest, but this is a mature business extracting growth through price-mix optimization and emerging market penetration. Dividend yield at 3.10% is well-covered by cash flows. The main friction is valuation: at 25.1x forward P/E versus a 5-year average of 24.5x, KO is slightly elevated, though PepsiCo trades at 26.3x so the premium to peers is actually negative -- KO is cheaper than PEP on this metric. Debt-to-equity of 1.75 looks high optically, but interest coverage at 9.5x means the debt load is manageable. The macro environment actually favors KO: in uncertain conditions, investors rotate into defensive consumer staples, and KO's global diversification buffers single-market slowdowns. Technically, price above both the 50-day SMA at 61.80 and 200-day SMA at 60.50 confirms a stable uptrend, and RSI at 58.2 is non-extended. Support at 60.00-60.50 is well-defined. The 12-plus month thesis is straightforward: buy a business with a durable moat, consistent cash generation, and rising dividend at a fair valuation. The forward P/E of 22.5x implies modest earnings growth expectations, which is achievable. KO qualifies as a core long-term holding.

NVDA at 895.50 is navigating a classic post-GTC sell-the-news dynamic. The stock hit 974.00 (all-time high) before pulling back; the daily MACD has crossed bearish (line -5.2 vs signal -2.1) and OBV showed negative divergence at the peak, meaning distribution was occurring even as price made new highs -- a meaningful warning sign. RSI cooling to 45.8 from above 75 is healthy but not yet at the oversold levels that typically signal a durable bottom. The 20-day EMA at 910.15 has flipped to resistance. The central tension is this: the short-term setup argues for continued weakness toward the 50-day EMA at 845.50, but the medium-term fundamental case remains overwhelmingly strong. Blackwell B200 GPU reception is highly positive and analysts project NVIDIA maintains 80%-plus share of AI accelerators. The next earnings report projects over 200% YoY revenue growth -- a beat-and-raise would likely ignite the next leg higher. The 200-day SMA sitting at 580.20 underscores just how powerful the primary uptrend is. Probability of further near-term consolidation to the 50-day EMA is 60%. A bull flag pattern is forming; confirmed breakout targets 1,050-1,100. For medium-term positioning over the next quarter, the pullback to test 845-880 is an opportunity rather than a threat. The ideal entry is near 50-day EMA support, with a base-case 3-month target of 1,050 and bull-case 1,150. The bear case of 780 requires either the 50-day EMA to fail or demand signals to deteriorate -- neither looks imminent.

NEE at 72.50 embodies the utility dilemma in a rising-rate environment: the regulated FPL segment provides predictable, bond-like cash flows while NEER (the renewable development arm) is capital-intensive and growth-sensitive, directly hurt by higher discount rates. These two profiles pull in opposite directions and the market is currently pricing the tension negatively. Technically, NEE is below the 20-day EMA at 74.10 and 50-day EMA at 75.50, MACD is bearish, and RSI at 38.5 is approaching oversold territory without yet showing a reversal. The 200-day SMA at 69.80 is the critical medium-term line; a sustained close below it would change the trend narrative materially. The rate-sensitivity is the dominant variable over 1-3 months. Higher Treasury yields compress the utility P/E multiple (utilities are valued largely on yield spread versus Treasuries), raise NEER's cost of capital, and reduce project economics on new wind and solar builds. The market is pricing at least one more rate hike, keeping a lid on the multiple. Medium-term base case (60% probability) is range-bound trading between 68 and 78. A soft inflation print causing the Fed to pause could push NEE back to 80 (25% probability). A break below the 200-day SMA targets 65 (15% probability). The long-term thesis through 12-plus months is intact: the Inflation Reduction Act provides multi-year NEER project visibility and FPL benefits from Florida's structural population growth. Dollar-cost averaging near 70 and selling covered calls at 80 is the sensible approach for patient long-term buyers.

DE at 375.50 sits at a technically critical juncture -- touching the lower Bollinger Band, approaching the RSI oversold zone at 38.5, and forming what appears to be a large descending triangle on the daily chart with flat support around 370-375 and a declining trendline near 395. The MACD at -2.15 below signal at -1.88 shows accelerating bearish momentum. The near-term risk is a breakdown below 370, which the descending triangle pattern flags explicitly; that would open a move toward 340-350. The base case (60%) is continued consolidation within the triangle between 370 and 395 until the next earnings report resolves the pattern. The fundamental tension is between cyclical macro headwinds and still-solid agricultural fundamentals. Deere faces concerns about global economic slowdown and sustained high rates dampening capex -- these weigh on sentiment for industrial cyclicals. But grain prices remain elevated, supporting farmer income and demand for new equipment ahead of North American planting season. The 200-day SMA at 398.50 is major overhead resistance capping significant rallies. In the medium term, the descending triangle is the dominant pattern. A bearish breakdown (25% probability) on negative macro data sends DE to 340-350. An upside surprise in earnings or a dovish Fed pivot (15% probability) triggers a breakout above 400 toward 420-430. The risk-reward for initiating longs here is asymmetric to the downside until the triangle resolves. The best tactical approach is to wait for triangle resolution post-earnings before committing capital, and use 369 as a hard stop if entering near current support.

MELI at 1,655.20 is a fascinating multi-layered story: an e-commerce and fintech leader in Latin America where currency translation -- specifically USD/BRL and USD/MXN -- acts as a constant, time-varying amplifier or damper on reported results. In the short term (1-7 days), technicals dominate and they are neutral: MACD barely negative (line -4.5 below signal), RSI at 47.8, and a Bollinger Band squeeze forming around the middle band at 1,660. The DXY is the key short-term watch variable -- a move above 105 would likely push MELI toward the 50-day EMA at 1,625. Over 1-3 months, the picture improves. An ascending triangle on the daily chart has resistance at 1,780-1,800, and price trades above the Ichimoku cloud, a structurally bullish configuration. A breakout above 1,800 targets approximately 2,000. The currency angle matters more at this horizon: a stabilizing or weakening USD versus BRL and MXN would directly boost MELI's reported USD revenue and EPS, acting as a meaningful tailwind. The Fintech segment (Mercado Pago) is the medium-term fundamental catalyst, with analysts expecting continued strong growth and margin expansion in Commerce. Over 6-12 months, MELI's secular positioning is compelling -- it is the dominant e-commerce and digital payments platform across Brazil, Mexico, and Argentina, operating in markets with rapidly growing internet penetration and formal financial system adoption. Long-term currency risk is real but mitigated by MELI's local-currency revenue generation. The 12-month bull case of 2,200-2,400 requires sustained EM macro stability and continued Mercado Pago monetization.

MU at 130.50 is positioned at an intersection of cyclical recovery and secular AI-driven structural demand. The short-term technicals are mildly cautious: RSI has pulled back from overbought territory to 62.5, MACD histogram is declining (line 2.85 vs signal 2.70), and price is pressing against the upper Bollinger Band at 132.10. The 20-day SMA at 125.40 is the key near-term support. A 60% probability of testing 128.00 support and a 40% probability of breaking above the 135 all-time high captures the short-term range well. The medium-term case is where MU's story becomes genuinely compelling. A potential bull flag on the daily chart targets 150 on breakout. The ADX at 45 confirms a very strong trend -- this is not a weak momentum stock. The fundamental drivers are aligned: DRAM and NAND ASPs are recovering as the memory cycle exits a cyclical trough, and analyst EPS revisions are trending upward for the next two quarters, which is historically a strong signal for semiconductor stocks. The HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) narrative is the most important medium-term catalyst. Micron is a key HBM supplier to NVIDIA GPU platforms, and that market is projected to grow at a 40%-plus CAGR. This creates a structural demand floor that differentiates MU from a pure cyclical play. Medium-term base case is 145-150 within 2-3 months, bull case 160-plus. Long-term (6-12 months), the 200-day EMA at 95.10 illustrates how far MU has run; a reversion of the cycle would be painful, but the HBM positioning provides a structural floor that prior memory cycles lacked. Best entry is a retest of 125-126 on any near-term pullback.

NFLX at 675.20 is in a short-term overbought condition -- RSI at 72.5 entering overbought territory, price pressing against the upper Bollinger Band at 680.10 -- but the underlying fundamental transformation underway is the dominant force for the medium and long term. Short-term, the overbought reading argues for a minor pullback toward the 665 support level (prior resistance, now support) or the 20-day EMA at 652.80 before the next leg higher. A direct break above 681 is possible but carries less favorable risk-reward without a pause. Medium-term, two structural catalysts are compounding: the ad-supported tier is growing faster than expected with high engagement and rising advertiser demand, and the password-sharing crackdown has successfully converted significant non-paying users into paying subscribers, directly boosting ARPU. These are not one-time events -- they represent a monetization architecture shift that will compound over multiple quarters. Price is in a clear ascending channel above the 50-day EMA at 635.40 and the 200-day EMA at 540.15; the volume shelf at 610-625 is now a robust support zone. Medium-term target of 730-750 within 3 months is plausible (75% confidence). Analyst estimates are being revised upward ahead of earnings, a positive sentiment backdrop. Long-term, the narrative hinges on content spend discipline and international expansion. The shift to advertising as a revenue stream is transformative -- it creates a second monetization engine and opens NFLX to a larger addressable market of ad-tolerant, price-sensitive subscribers. The risk is content cost inflation and intensifying competition from Disney-plus and Apple TV-plus.

NVDA's 10-for-1 stock split is largely a psychological event -- it does not change the underlying economics -- but its effects on near-term price action are real. Post-split price around 121 reflects the split-adjusted level from approximately 1,210 pre-split, and the 200%-plus volume surge confirms broad retail participation responding to the lower nominal price. RSI at 68 on the daily is elevated but not yet technically overbought, and the stock trades significantly above its 20-day EMA at roughly 112 post-split, confirming the primary uptrend is intact. A minor pullback to 115-118 (60% probability) would be healthy before the next leg. The medium-term case is where the analysis gets substantive. The fundamental backdrop is exceptional: analysts forecast Data Center revenue above 25 billion dollars for the upcoming quarter versus 22.6 billion last quarter, another massive sequential step-up. The Blackwell architecture transition (B100/B200) is the critical product cycle catalyst -- any updates on production ramps and customer adoption timelines will move the stock. Forward P/E at roughly 45x sounds rich in isolation, but with 90%-plus EPS growth forecasted, the PEG ratio of approximately 1.0 suggests growth is fairly priced. Base-case 3-month target is 145-150 on continued earnings momentum. Bull case of 160-plus requires both a significant beat and upward guidance revision. Bear case of roughly 105 (50-day EMA) requires either demand deceleration signals or a broad market correction -- neither looks imminent given the AI capital expenditure cycle. The split removes the nominal price barrier and broadens the shareholder base, which is a modest but genuine structural positive for liquidity.

CRM at 225.50 is at a technically neutral inflection point -- RSI at 46.8, price oscillating around the middle Bollinger Band at 226.10, MACD barely negative (line -0.45 vs signal -0.41). The stock is consolidating after pulling back from 235 resistance, and the most likely near-term path is continued range-bound trading between 222 and 228. The 50-day EMA at 218.50 is the critical support below that range. The medium-term thesis rests on two questions: whether Slack integration is yielding revenue synergies, and whether operating margins are expanding or being compressed by the acquisition cost drag. At 55x forward P/E, CRM is priced for flawless execution -- any guidance disappointment could trigger a sharp re-rating. The positive indicators are a projected 21% YoY revenue growth for the upcoming quarter and Remaining Performance Obligation (RPO) trends, which serve as the leading indicator for future revenue recognition. A bull flag or pennant is potentially forming; a breakout above 235 targets 255-260 via measured move. The Ichimoku cloud test at current levels is important -- price is sitting on the top of the daily cloud, which is support. A break below the cloud would shift the medium-term outlook negative. Base case (60%): consolidation resolves upward, stock grinds toward 250 over 2-3 months. Bull case (25%): Slack synergies surprise positively, earnings beat triggers a move to 265. Bear case (15%): margin disappointment and slowing RPO growth send CRM to 200-205. The 200-day SMA at 205.15 is the long-term bull-bear line.

NVDA at 905.50 is showing early signs of short-term exhaustion after a parabolic advance. The MACD has crossed below its signal line (15.2 vs 16.8, histogram -1.6), RSI has cooled from 85 to 62, and price has pulled back inside the upper Bollinger Band after trading along it for weeks -- all consistent with a mean-reversion move toward the 20-day SMA at 875. Volume on recent down days has been below average, which is a mild positive: heavy distribution selling has not yet materialized. A test of 875 (20-day EMA) within the next week is the 60% probability scenario. For medium-term investors this is the relevant entry point. The 50-day EMA at 790 and 200-day EMA at 580 confirm how powerful the primary uptrend is -- any pullback into the 875-875 zone is shallow within that broader context. The fundamental setup for the next 1-3 months is compelling: Data Center revenue is projected to grow 350% YoY in the upcoming earnings report, Blackwell B200 architecture announcements have been universally positive from analyst coverage, and the forward P/E of 38x with a PEG ratio of approximately 1.1 suggests the valuation is demanding but justifiable if growth is delivered. The bull flag forming on the daily chart targets 1,050 on breakout. Base case (65%): consolidation in 850-950 range before earnings, then breakout toward 1,050. Bull case (25%): blowout earnings propel to 1,100-plus. Bear case (10%): earnings miss sends to 50-day EMA around 790. Strategy differentiation by profile: active traders enter near 875 with stop at 865; long-term investors already holding should not act on short-term noise.

NVDA at 120.50 (post-split adjusted) is in a technically extreme condition: RSI at 88.5 is deep overbought, MACD is significantly extended above its signal line (5.80 vs 4.95), and price is trading above the upper Bollinger Band at 115.70 -- that last condition alone assigns a 70% probability to a near-term pullback toward the 115-116 zone. Declining volume on the last two up-days confirms weakening conviction at these levels. This is not a long entry setup. Short-term, the path of least resistance is a reversion toward the 20-period EMA at approximately 112.50 on the 4-hour chart. A tactical short with tight stop above 122.50 targeting 115 is the aggressive play, though it cuts against a powerful uptrend, which makes it a lower-conviction trade. Medium-term, the picture flips entirely constructive. A Golden Cross was confirmed last month (50-day EMA above 200-day EMA), OBV is in a steep uptrend confirming institutional accumulation, and the 50-day EMA at 98.20 is well-supported. Analysts expect Q2 revenue of 28 billion dollars (+105% YoY) and EPS of 0.62 (+130% YoY) -- with high potential for another beat-and-raise. The Blackwell platform launch is the next product-cycle catalyst. Medium-term base case is 135 (+12%), bull case 145 (+20%), bear case a correction to the 50-day EMA around 100 (-17%). Probability distribution: 65% base case, 25% bullish, 10% bearish. The short-term overbought condition does not change the medium and long-term bull thesis -- it simply argues against chasing here.

PLTR at 24.50 is consolidating after a strong post-earnings rally, and the setup has multiple constructive characteristics. RSI at 58.2 is neutral-to-bullish after cooling from overbought above 70. MACD is above signal but histogram is diminishing -- consolidation, not reversal. Bollinger Bands are constricting around the middle band, which is a coiling precursor to a directional move. Volume declining over the last three sessions supports the consolidation thesis. The critical near-term levels are 24.10 (20-period EMA on 4-hour chart, immediate support) and 23.50 (previous breakout level, structural support). Resistance is at 25.25 (recent high) and 26.00 (psychological). A bull flag pattern on the daily chart targets 29.00 on confirmed breakout above 25.25. The medium-term fundamental case is strengthening: Q1 commercial revenue accelerated to 40% YoY growth, management raised full-year guidance, and the upcoming AIPCon event is a concrete catalyst for new contract announcements and product showcases that historically have moved the stock. PLTR trades at a premium valuation that demands continued high-growth delivery, but the 40% commercial growth rate supports the multiple. The 50-day EMA at 22.15 and 200-day EMA at 18.90 frame the long-term bull structure -- any medium-term pullback to 22-23 would be a high-conviction add zone for long-term holders. Long-term (6-12 months), the government AI contract pipeline and commercial AIP adoption are the twin structural growth drivers. The 27.50 previous multi-year high is the next major resistance after 26.00.

SO at 72.50 is a textbook rate-sensitive utility analysis. The Southern Company's investment case is almost entirely a function of where 10-year Treasury yields are heading, and the stock's near-term movements will track yield changes tick-for-tick. RSI at 51.2 is perfectly neutral, Bollinger Bands are contracting, MACD is flat -- all consistent with a stock awaiting a macro trigger rather than exhibiting internal momentum. Short-term, the trading range of 71.80 to 73.00 is likely to hold absent a macro catalyst. The most significant medium-term catalyst is a confirmed dovish Fed pivot -- the market is pricing potential rate cuts within 3-6 months, and confirmation would revalue SO's 3.9% dividend yield favorably relative to Treasuries. The removal of the Vogtle nuclear plant construction overhang is a meaningful fundamental positive: that project was a multi-billion dollar cost overrun that weighed on SO's balance sheet and earnings quality for years. With it complete, focus shifts to operational efficiency and regulated earnings growth from Vogtle Unit 4 contribution. A Golden Cross (50-day EMA at 71.50 above 200-day EMA at 69.80) is the technical bullish signal. An ascending triangle on the daily chart targets 78-80 on a breakout above 74.50. For long-term income investors, SO offers 3.9% yield with 2-3% annual dividend growth -- a total return profile of approximately 6-7% annually, which is competitive in a utility context. The key risk is rates staying elevated, which would keep the dividend spread compressed and the multiple capped.

LVMUY at 158.20 is caught in a China-driven sell-off, and the technical picture is unambiguously negative in the near term. The MACD has crossed below its signal line (line -1.55), RSI is at 38.5 approaching oversold, price has pierced the lower Bollinger Band at 159.10, and volume has surged 40% above the 20-day average on down days -- that combination signals bearish conviction, not a washout bottom. The 200-day SMA at 155.00 is the key medium-term support; a break below it would activate a potential head and shoulders pattern with a neckline at 155, targeting 140-145 on measured move. The 70% probability of testing 155 near-term feels well-calibrated. The fundamental case for concern is substantial. Greater China represents 25-30% of LVMH's total revenue. A sustained 10% regional demand decline would reduce group revenue by 2.5-3.0%, and due to high operating leverage on a 68% gross margin business, the earnings impact would be proportionally larger -- roughly 5-7% net profit hit. Analysts are revising Q3-Q4 revenue growth from 12% YoY down to 6-8%, and a promotional environment to clear Asian inventory could pressure those gross margins further. LVMH's brand equity (Vuitton, Dior, Hennessy) provides long-run pricing power, but that structural strength does not protect against a cyclical China slowdown in the 1-3 month window. Long-term, at 12-18 months, if China demand stabilizes or recovers, LVMUY's aspirational brand positioning at scale is a buy. Near term, the risk-reward does not support initiating a position until the 155 level holds or breaks decisively.

NVDA at 905.50 is in the classic post-earnings gap-up situation: powerful move confirmed by 150% of 20-day average volume on the gap day, followed by declining volume on subsequent sessions -- the buying wave has passed and the stock is digesting. RSI at 78.5 is deep overbought, price is trading well above the upper Bollinger Band, MACD histogram is expanding but the steepness is unsustainable. Base case (60%) is consolidation between 880-920 as the stock builds a new base; a retest of 855 (top of pre-earnings consolidation) is the 30% scenario. The fundamental justification for the move is real: Q4 earnings beat with revenue +265% YoY, and Q1 guidance came in significantly above consensus -- this is genuine hyper-growth, not multiple expansion on flat earnings. The upcoming GTC conference (March 18-21) is the next major catalyst: Blackwell B200 GPU and AI strategy announcements that could reset analyst targets again. Forward P/E of 35x with a PEG of approximately 1.1 is demanding but defensible given 30%-plus projected EPS growth. Medium-term base case target is 1,000-1,050 within 2-3 months (65% probability). The resolution of the short-term/long-term conflict is straightforward: short-term overbought signals are noise within a structural bull market in AI infrastructure. Do not short the trend; do find better entries during consolidation. The 850-860 zone is the ideal medium-term entry point -- it represents both the Bollinger Band middle and a high-volume VPVR node, making it robust support.

PLTR at 24.85 is in what appears to be a textbook breakout setup: Bollinger Band width at a 3-month low of 0.08 (extreme squeeze), RSI at 52.3 (neutral, loaded with potential), MACD near flat and perfectly intertwined with signal line (zero directional bias), and volume 35% below 20-day average (classic drying-up before a breakout). Every technical indicator is pointing toward an imminent large move. The only missing piece is direction. The consolidation ceiling is 25.30 and the floor is 24.50; a daily close above 25.30 on high volume is the long trigger, targeting 26.00-26.50. A close below 24.50 is the short trigger, targeting 23.80. The 60/40 probability split favoring the upside breakout is supported by OBV trending higher during the consolidation -- accumulation is occurring while price is flat, which is classically bullish. A rumored government contract announcement is the potential spark. The medium-term picture via bullish pennant on the daily chart targets 29.00 on confirmed breakout, with the 50-day EMA at 23.10 providing robust support below. The long-term AI thesis deserves acknowledgment: PLTR operates an AI-driven data analytics platform with structural moats in both government intelligence contracts and commercial enterprise software. The 200-day EMA at 19.50 illustrates the scale of the longer-term move. The tension between the high valuation and the growth narrative is real, but the near-term question is simply: will 25.30 break first or 24.50? The technical setup is clean; wait for the trigger.

FSLR at 262.50 presents a valuation-versus-growth conflict that resolves cleanly when you use the right metric. The trailing P/E of 31x creates a misleading headline; the forward P/E of 21x and a PEG ratio of 0.8 (using 35-40% projected EPS growth) actually suggest FSLR is undervalued relative to its growth trajectory. The IRA's 45X manufacturing tax credit is the key structural variable -- it directly subsidizes FSLR as the only major non-Chinese crystalline-silicon competitor in the US market, turning a policy tailwind into a durable earnings uplift with multi-year visibility through the company's 2026 project backlog. Short-term technicals argue for patience: RSI at 71.5 is overbought, MACD histogram is declining (momentum slowing), price is near the upper Bollinger Band at 268, and volume has been fading over 3 sessions. A pullback to the 20-day EMA at 248.50 is the 60% probability near-term scenario and the better entry point. Medium-term, the chart setup is constructive: price above the 50-day EMA at 221.70 and 200-day EMA at 175.40, with a bull flag formation targeting 310-320 on breakout above 270. The 15% QoQ revenue growth guidance and a robust backlog with forward visibility confirm the fundamental support. For the 6-12 month horizon, FSLR's competitive moat -- domestic manufacturing, cadmium-telluride technology independent of Chinese polysilicon supply chains, and IRA-anchored economics -- is durable. The ideal entry is 245-255; target 295-305 medium-term and 320-plus long-term.

LLY at 885.10 is walking the upper Bollinger Band with RSI at 68.5 -- a sign of powerful momentum but also proximity to the point where pullbacks become more likely. The MACD histogram is shrinking (line 12.5 vs signal 11.8) and volume is below its 20-day average, suggesting the upward thrust is decelerating. The 855.20 level (20-day SMA) is the first real support, and the 810.75 (50-day EMA) is the medium-term bull-bear line. The fundamental tension at LLY is between a 65x forward P/E -- priced for perfection -- and genuinely exceptional growth from the GLP-1 franchise. Zepbound and Mounjaro are not niche products; they represent a paradigm shift in obesity and diabetes treatment with massive global addressable markets. Analysts project 25%-plus YoY revenue growth for the upcoming quarter. The key risk to the bull thesis is a supply constraint: LLY has repeatedly been unable to fully meet demand for tirzepatide-based products, which both caps revenue realization and creates vulnerability if a competitor (Novo Nordisk's semaglutide) gains preference in the formulary negotiation cycle. At 65x forward earnings, any negative revision to the growth narrative -- competitor trial results, safety headlines, pricing pressure from Medicare negotiation -- could cause a sharp multiple compression. The bull flag targeting 950-960 is technically valid and well-supported. Long-term, the donanemab Alzheimer's data and next-generation GLP-1 (oral formulations) are pipeline optionality. But the immediate risk-reward for new longs at 885 is asymmetric to the downside; better to enter on a pullback toward 855 or 810.
